function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you set up the Dockerfile, Kubernetes manifests, and GitHub‑Actions workflow for the **zelarhq/nodejs‑welcome** repository.  
Below you’ll find:

1. A suggested `Dockerfile` (based on a typical Node.js “Hello World” app).  
2. A minimal `k8s/deployment.yaml` + `k8s/service.yaml`.  
3. A `.github/workflows/build.yml` that builds the image and pushes it to GitHub Container Registry whenever you push to `main`.

> **NOTE** – I don’t have the ability to run `git clone`, `git add`, `git commit`, or `git push` from here, so you’ll need to run those commands locally after you’ve added the files.

---

## 1. Suggested `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
# ------------------------------------
# Base image: official Node.js LTS (alpine variant)
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set working directory inside the container
WORKDIR /usr/src/app

# Copy only the package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the application code
COPY . .

# Expose the port your app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Default command to start the app
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *Why this Dockerfile?*  
> - Uses the lightweight `node:18-alpine` image.  
> - Copies `package.json`/`package-lock.json` first so Docker can cache the dependency layer.  
> - Installs only production dependencies (`npm ci --only=production`).  
> - Exposes port `3000` (the default for many Node.js examples).  
> - Starts the app with `node app.js`.

If the repo uses a different entry point (e.g., `npm start`), adjust the `CMD` accordingly.

---

## 2. Kubernetes Manifests

Create a folder called `k8s/` at the root of the repo and add two files:

### `k8s/deployment.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/<YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace <YOUR_GITHUB_USERNAME>
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

### `k8s/service.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer   # Change to NodePort or ClusterIP if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # External port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> **Tip** – If you’re deploying to a cluster that doesn’t support `LoadBalancer` (e.g., Minikube), change `type` to `NodePort` and note the assigned node port.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow

Create a file at `.github/workflows/build.yml`:

```yaml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write   # Needed to push to GHCR

    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Cache Docker layers
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: /tmp/.buildx-cache
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-${{ github.sha }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-buildx-

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        file: Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What this does**  
> - Triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> - Logs into GHCR using the built‑in `GITHUB_TOKEN`.  
> - Builds the image from the root `Dockerfile`.  
> - Tags it as `ghcr.io/<owner>/nodejs-welcome:latest`.  
> - Pushes the image to GitHub Packages.

---

## 4. Add, Commit, Push

Once you’ve added the files above:

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/*.yaml .github/workflows/build.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

Your GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run on the next push to `main`, building and publishing the image.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | `Dockerfile` added at repo root |
| ✅ | `k8s/deployment.yaml` & `k8s/service.yaml` added |
| ✅ | `.github/workflows/build.yml` added |
| ✅ | Files committed & pushed |
